title: The Two Mysteries Shown Daily in the Sun: The Going-Forth and the Gathering
reading:
Know what is being shown to you: two great mysteries are made plain every day in the same sun that gives light, one in its rising and one in its setting. Look at them.

When the Lord's illumining wisdom is about to shine forth into the natural mind, every creature of flesh — every appetite, every disordered affection that has been claiming its life from the natural and feeding on its own — recoils from that Radiance and draws back into the hiding-places where it had been at home. The whole multitude of the natural mind shuts its mouth; the night that had covered it gathers itself in and withdraws into its own recesses. This is what happens at the first contest of regeneration: when the Lord first comes forth as the Divine Human into the soul that has been organized by self-love, his light falls upon every form of the proprium at once, and they come out of the storehouses and powers and dwellings they had built for themselves, are dislodged from the deep places they had occupied, and the body in which the proprium's whole fivefold operation had been mounted is undone. That undoing is the first contest, and the rising of the sun in the soul is its sign.

Then look at the evening, when the sun is about to set out of the natural mind. All the people, and the affections that go with them, withdraw to their hiding-places and their houses and conceal themselves. This too is a sign — the sign of the end, of how things will stand at the consummation of the natural mind. For when all that is the Lord's has at last been recognized as his and refined out, when every claim has been laid off and every thing dissolved, the final gathering will draw what is the Lord's inward into the full image of completion. That is the close of the day. At that hour the last gathering goes upward into light, and what had been the enemy — the proprium claiming itself, the death that came of self-love — goes into the place of judgment, together with the souls that have loved the darkness and the speech that denied the Lord; they go in with it into the region where the sun does not shine, and there they remain, in the state to which they have given themselves, while of the soul that is raised it can be said: a light shines for it.

These are the two mysteries the Lord shows daily in the same illumining wisdom that radiates over the soul: the going-forth that scatters every claimed thing, and the gathering that brings every recognized thing home.
